issues.legal_issue: A plaint in a separate suit alleging an already concluded contract, and service of that plaint, did not constitute acceptance and communication of an unaccepted offer to assign a lease.
material_facts: The offer to assign the lease was not supported by consideration for a promise to keep it open, so it could be revoked before acceptance.

Before the revocation reached the offerees, they filed a plaint in a separate possession suit alleging that the assignment contract had already been concluded and reserving their right to bring a suit for specific performance.
The plaint was served on the offeror before the revocation reached the offerees, but the offerees made no other oral or written acceptance before then.
The later suit for specific performance was brought after the offer had been withdrawn.
issues.conclusion: The plaint in the separate suit was neither an acceptance of the offer nor a communication of acceptance. As no acceptance was made before the offer was revoked, there was no concluded contract and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(6), 3 and 7 of the Contract Act, acceptance must be an acceptance of the offer and must be communicated; mere mental assent is insufficient. An offer unsupported by consideration for a promise to keep it open may be revoked before acceptance. The Court distinguished Boys v. Ayerst, Agar v. Biden and Bloxam's case, and applied In re Pellatt's case. It observed that the old Chancery practice treating the filing of a specific-performance bill as acceptance could not be applied to a plaint in a separate suit that was not intended to accept the offer.

rule.if: specific_performance_appeal and offer_keep_open_promise_unsupported and no_other_acceptance_before_revocation and separate_suit_plaint_not_acceptance and plaint_service_not_acceptance_communication and revocation_reached_offeree_before_specific_performance_suit

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged contract.
predicates.offer_keep_open_promise_unsupported: The offeror stated that the offer would remain open, but the offeree gave no consideration for that promise.
predicates.no_other_acceptance_before_revocation: The offeree made no oral or written acceptance apart from the separate-suit plaint before the revocation reached the offeree.
predicates.separate_suit_plaint_not_acceptance: The offeree's plaint in a separate suit alleged that a contract already existed rather than accepting the offer.
predicates.plaint_service_not_acceptance_communicat: Service through the court of the separate-suit plaint did not communicate an acceptance of the offer.
predicates.revocation_reached_offeree_before_specif: The revocation reached the offeree before the offeree brought the suit seeking specific performance.

issues.definition: When an unsupported promise to keep an offer open is followed by no effective acceptance before revocation, a separate-suit plaint that does not accept the offer and its service do not create a concluded contract.
